 Everything We Are Watching This Week (November 16-22): Suryaa, Ebenezer & More 
 Everything We Are Watching This Week (November 16-22): Suryaa, Ebenezer & More
 Written by Siddharth Thampi Updated on Nov 16, 2026, 13:27 IST 
 Follow On Select as Preferred on This week is packed with some explosive tales from Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak to Ebenezer & more. Here is everything to watch: 
We’ve finally reached the third week of November, but the fun is nowhere close to over. This week is packed with an explosive set of releases ranging from a retired police officer facing an organ trafficking organisation to  a group of unhinged robbers making viral sensation videos out of their heists, among many other stories. Here is everything we are watching this week (November 16-22). 
 In This Article 
 Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak 
 Godzilla Minus Zero 
 O.M. Operation Mole 
 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping 
 How To Rob a Bank 
 Ebenezer 
 Nanhey Dil 
 Good Partner 2 
 Party Animals 
 The Blue Road 
 Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak 
 Director: M. Padmakumar 
 Cast: Sunny Deol, Ravi Kishan, Pragya Jaiswal, Manish Wadhwa, Tanushree Chakraborty, Tinnu Anand 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 In Suryaa, a retired police officer, Soorya Pratap Singh (Sunny Deol), is reeled back into a murder investigation after the demise of his wife. Digging deeper to excavate the truth, he finds himself in the midst of a dangerous criminal web, uncovering a system of medical organ trafficking. 
 Godzilla Minus Zero 
 Director: Takashi Yamazaki 
 Cast: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yuki Yamada, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Sakura Ando 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Godzilla Minus Zero acts as the direct sequel, taking place two years after the events of Godzilla Minus One. Set in the year 1949, we will once again see the Shikishima family reprise their roles in a world where a new threat is introduced in the form of King Ghidorah, as the new antagonist for Godzilla. 
 O.M. Operation Mole 
 Director: Rajkumar Periasamy 
 Cast: Dhanush, Mammooty, Sai Pallavi, Sree Leela, Naseeruddin Shah 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 Under the direction of Rajkumar Periasamy, O.M. Operation Mole is an action-crime thriller inspired by real-life incidents surrounding the smuggling of sandalwood from the forests of Tiruvanamalai. The plot of the narrative centres on a high-stakes police investigation called Operation Mole, led by IPS officer Nithya Reddy (Sai Pallavi), with a woodcutter (Dhanush) entering the smuggling network as an undercover spy to extract crucial insider information. Leading the shady operation is the kingpin Burma Karthikeyan (Mammooty). 
 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping 
 Director: Francis Lawrence 
 Cast: Jennifer Lawrence, Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Ralph Fiennes 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 The popular franchise is all set to embark on a different route this time with its upcoming release, Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. Instead of following up with yet another sequel, they will be winding the clock back. All the way back to 24 years prior to the Hunger Games Trilogy in the fictional world of Panem, on the morning of the 50th Annual Hunger Games. The focus stays on this edition of the infamous event, following the journey of a 16-year-old boy named Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the brutal test of survival he endures. 
 How To Rob a Bank 
 Director: David Leitch   
 Cast: Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Pete Davidson, John C. Reilly 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 Under the visionary direction of David Leitch, How To Rob a Bank will showcase the lives of a group of unconventional criminals. Why unconventional, you ask? While masking themselves under the avatars of robbers, their main agenda isn’t to become rich doing so but to leave a message.
In a way, you are reminded of Jackie Chan’s New Police Story, with the difference being that the robbers here upload their videos online to become viral sensations, creating a massive cult following. The plot thickens further when a desperate cop begins to track them down. Regardless of the heat they’ve generated, they aspire to complete one of their most ambitious robberies. 
 Ebenezer 
 Director: Ti West 
 Cast: Johnny Depp, Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Ian McKellen, Sam Claflin   
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 Johny Depp is back once again, this time adding a completely new avatar to his list of famous makeovers. In Ebenezer, he will be playing the role of Ebenezer in this thrilling ghost story surrounding a plot of redemption. Living a life of misery and loneliness, on Christmas Eve, he is visited by a chain-bound ghost, Jacob Marley, who talks to him about one final attempt at escaping a miserable afterlife. In this fun fantasy narrative, Ebenezer is guided by the spirits to his past, present, and future, where he gets to confront his buried memories, face his wrongdoings, and have a chance of rewiring his ways. 
 Nanhey Dil 
 Director: Swarupraj Medara 
 Cast: Suniel Shetty, Sarvesh Adawade, Sarvar Ahuja, Vrushali Hatalkar 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 Nanhey Dil will explore the life of children and how pure persistence can break the mould of social and economic barriers, echoing a warm message of ambition and courage in this family-friendly story. Suniel Shetty will feature in this movie, where he plays the role of a principal at a prestigious school, seeing potential in a bright young middle-class boy named Raghu, and providing him with an opportunity to study alongside students from privileged families. 
 Good Partner 2 
 Director: Seo Min-jung 
 Cast: Jang Na-ra, Kim Hye-yoon, Pyo Ji-hoon, Park Hae-jin 
 Platform: Viki 
 Release Date: November 20
 The sequel to Good Partner is underway, this time focusing on the divorce lawyer Cha Eun-Kyung (Jang Na-ra), who is entering a new phase of her career. After leaving her previous law firm, she sets up her own practice, Libon, with a single ambition of scaling it from the ground up. To start adding blocks to this dream, she hires Kang Hye-seong (Kim Hye-hoon), who is an experienced divorce lawyer possessing a unique approach with respect to handling her cases. With contrasting personalities, they must find a way to work together and take on the challenging cases that come their way. 
 Party Animals 
 Director: Ravi Chhabriya 
 Cast: Viraj Ghelani, Arjun Tanwar, Alam Taqveem Khan, Soundous Moufakir, Pragati Nagpal, Jaanya Joshi, Naqiyah Haji, Kamlesh Sawant 
 Platform: Theatrical Release 
 Release Date: November 20
 Party Animals is the story of one crazy night featuring an ensemble of unique characters from different phases of their life, their paths intertwining with each other to create a situation of chaos. Having taken two different paths in their career, Mann (Viraj Ghelani) and Armaan (Arjun Tanwar) meet up in Mumbai to celebrate a fun party night, which quickly spirals into a night of brewing confusion. With fun waster eggs, fourth-wall breaks, and abundant cameos, this will be a fun watch for you and your friends. 
 The Blue Road 
 Director:  Han Jun-hee 
 Cast: Son Suk-ku, Nagayama Eita, Kim Shin-rok 
 Platform: Netflix 
 Release Date: November 20
 The Blue Road is an upcoming crime thriller. In a fun mix, it merges the journeys of a Korean and Japanese detective as they investigate a series of brutal murders being committed across the two countries. The trail of incidents begins in Tokyo, with more hints of a similar case being uncovered in Korea, making the pattern as clear as daylight. Detectives Kim Seok (Son Suk-ku) and Inose (Nagayama Eita) must join forces to track down and capture the deranged serial killer, their mindsets contrasting with one another, probing them to handle the case in ways they deem right in their terms.
